The witness covers Format 1 and Format 2 with DEPENDING on a random-access file only.

reader.notes: A pointer rule: the relative FD reuses the sequential RECORD clause, and the compiler applies the same RecordClauseRules table and the same keyed-connector size rule to a relative file. Each syntax rule is refused with a §1985 citation, and the run-time rules give 44 and the DEPENDING length. Format 3 is read back as a variable-length record of its own size (GR13 leaves that choice to the implementor).

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-131/c6.cob (relative FD, RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON DL, where 01 G. 05 DL PIC 99 OCCURS 3 TIMES) compiles EXIT 0 at --std 85, and at --std 2023 too. Run probe g9c.cob (runs/g9c-001, --std 85): FD RT RECORD VARYING FROM 2 TO 8 DEPENDING ON TL, TL a table element; MOVE 5 TO TL(1), WRITE RT-REC answers 00 and the record reads back as all 8 characters '12345678', and after the successful READ TL is still 00,00,00. So the DEPENDING item is accepted and then silently ignored: GR10a (write length from data-name-1) and GR11 (length stored after READ) are not performed for it. Under the 1985 text the reference is illegal: 'Each table element reference must be subscripted except when such reference appears' in USE FOR DEBUGGING, a SEARCH subject, REDEFINES, OCCURS KEY IS (none is the RECORD clause), so data-name-1 can never be a table element and the FD must be refused. RecordClauseRules.Rules' three SR-13.18.43.3-6 rows (Of1985 VII.3.8.3 SR4) test IsElementary, the integer picture and the section only, never a table element. The same mechanism was fixed for VALUE OF data-name-1 in kb/Work PB5299 (DataItem.IsTableElement, COBOL6849); the RECORD clause DEPENDING operand is the sibling that sweep did not reach. Everything else the reader claimed held: c1 'RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE CHARACTERS', c2 'RECORD 4 TO 8', c3 'RECORD 8', c4 'VARYING TO 8 DEPENDING ON', c5 qualified 'DL OF G', c10 'DEPENDING DL' with a COMP item all compile; c7 (ZZ9) and c9 (X(2)) refused COBOL2922 SR4; c8 RECORD CONTAINS 0 refused COBOL2386 (III.2); g9b-002 at 85: RL unchanged by REWRITE/START/DELETE (GR9), a 30 length write 44, Format 2 without FROM/TO takes min 3 max 9 from the record descriptions (2 and 10 give 44, GR6/GR7). cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.3.2.4 GR5 (the text is in GR5); OK §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR4 (the text is in SR4); OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4 (the text is in SR4); OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10 (the text is in GR10); OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR11 (the text is in GR11).
